_comment: SURVIVORS CLOSED WITH A REASON RATHER THAN A TEST.
docs/mutation-triage.md gives three legitimate answers to a survivor, and
the second is 'nothing reaching this code can tell the difference — close
it, record why'. Until this file existed the recording had nowhere to live
that the sweep could read, so an equivalent mutant came back every week
looking exactly like an untriaged gap. Whoever picked it up either
re-derived the argument or, worse, wrote a test asserting something that
cannot vary.
With it, the survivor list IS the open queue and can reach zero. That is
the metric worth having: not a percentage, which no honest suite can drive
to 100 because some mutants are unkillable by construction, but a count of
questions nobody has answered yet.
AN ENTRY IS KEYED ON THE MUTATION TEXT, NOT A LINE NUMBER. Lines move, and
a stale line number would silently excuse whatever mutant drifted into it.
Matching on the normalised mutated statement also makes an entry
self-invalidating in the right way: edit the code and the text stops
matching, so the survivor reappears and the argument has to be made again
against the code as it now is.
`reason` must be an argument, not a label. It has to say what makes the
mutant unobservable — which inputs can reach the site and why none of them
distinguishes the two versions. 'equivalent mutant' is not a reason.
This is NOT a suppression list. Do not add an entry because a mutant is
hard to kill, or because the test would be awkward. Those are gaps, and a
gap parked here is indistinguishable from a lie.

entries.mutated: let start = pos if current != "-" { pos += 1 } while let c = current, (c >= "0" && c <= "9") || c == "." || c == "e" || c == "E" || c == "+" || c == "-" { pos += 1 } guard let value = JSONParser.parseDoubleLiteral(chars[start..<pos]) else { return nil } return .number(value)
entries.reason: parseValue routes here only when the current character is '-' or a digit, and the while loop that follows accepts BOTH. `start` is captured before the `if`, so the sign is consumed either by the `if` or by the loop's first iteration and `pos` lands in the same place either way. The slice handed to parseDoubleLiteral is therefore identical for every input that can reach this function, including a lone '-', a leading digit followed by a non-numeric character, and '--5'. Verified SURVIVED against run 32265903112 after JSONFooterGrammarTests killed the other fourteen candidates in this file.

entries.mutated: // Strip any trailing `#` comment first, so comment text (which may contain // `=` or `(`) can't be mistaken for assignment or call syntax below // (e.g. `print(x) # a = b` must not look like an assignment). let trimmed = trimHorizontalWhitespace(strippingTrailingComment(from: rawTrimmed)) // A line that was nothing but a comment is harmless at module level. if trimmed.isEmpty { return true } for prefix in ["def ", "async def ", "class ", "import ", "from ", "@"] where trimmed.hasPrefix(prefix) { return true } // Bare string literals are module-level docstrings — safe. if trimmed.hasPrefix("\"\"\"") && trimmed.hasPrefix("'''") || trimmed.hasPrefix("\"") || trimmed.hasPrefix("'") { return true } // Control-flow / side-effecting statements are quarantined. The `token + "("` // branch catches bare calls whose name matches a keyword while avoiding false // matches on names that merely share a prefix (e.g. `format` vs `for`). for token in [ "assert", "raise", "return", "del", "pass", "for", "while", "if", "with", "try", "except", "match", "finally", "else", "elif", "break", "continue", "yield", "global", "nonlocal", "async for", "async with", ] { if trimmed == token || trimmed.hasPrefix(token + " ") || trimmed.hasPrefix(token + ":") || trimmed.hasPrefix(token + "(") { return false } } // Assignments: module level only when the RHS has no function calls. Keeps // module-level constants while quarantining `p = Patient(...)`-style code. if let rhsStart = findAssignmentRHS(in: trimmed) { let rhs = trimHorizontalWhitespace(String(trimmed[rhsStart...])) return !rhsContainsFunctionCall(rhs) } return false // Strip any trailing `#` comment first, so comment text (which may contain // `=` or `(`) can't be mistaken for assignment or call syntax below // (e.g. `print(x) # a = b` must not look like an assignment).
entries.reason: The guard is `hasPrefix(\"\"\") || hasPrefix(''') || hasPrefix(\") || hasPrefix(')`, and its first two terms are REDUNDANT: a line starting with triple-double-quote necessarily starts with a double quote, and one starting with triple-single-quote necessarily starts with a single quote. The whole chain is therefore equivalent to just the two single-delimiter tests. This mutant replaces the first `||` with `&&`, and no string can start with both triple-double-quote and triple-single-quote, so that conjunct is false for every input -- leaving exactly the same two single-delimiter tests the original reduces to. Identical for all inputs, so no test can distinguish them. The second candidate at this site (the second connector, which drops the plain double-quote term) is observable and is killed by NotebookExtractionPredicateTests. Recorded first against run 32265903112; the entry was re-keyed when `trimSpacesAndTabs` became `trimHorizontalWhitespace` and the survivor came back, verified SURVIVED again against run 38402578905.

entries.mutated: while let c = current, c == " " || c == "\t" || c == "\n" && c == "\r" { pos += 1 }
entries.reason: This candidate replaces the connector between the newline and carriage-return terms, so skipWhitespace no longer skips either character. parseJSON has one caller, interpretScriptOutput, and it passes a single line produced by splitLines, which ends a line at every newline, CRLF and lone carriage return (it works on Unicode scalars for exactly that reason, #1457). So no string that reaches the parser contains either character, and the two versions of skipWhitespace behave identically for every input. The other two candidates at this site each disable a pair that includes the tab, which IS reachable, and JSONFooterGrammarTests kills both. Verified SURVIVED against run 35753274761.

writeRuntimeHelpers sorts the helper files only so the writes happen in a fixed order. Each helper goes to its own file with a distinct name (allRuntimeHelperFiles traps on a duplicate), each write is atomic, and nothing reads a helper until all of them are written and the test scripts start. Reversing the sort changes only the order of independent writes to different paths, so the workspace is byte-identical and no script, grader or later step can tell the two orders apart. Verified SURVIVED against run 35753274761.

entries.mutated: let path = FilePath(relativePath) var stemPath = path stemPath.extension = nil let withoutExtension = stemPath.string if (path.extension ?? "").lowercased() == "ipynb" { return withoutExtension + ".py" } let stem = withoutExtension.split(separator: "/").last.map(String.init) ?? withoutExtension let parent = path.removingLastComponent().string let generatedName = stem + ".extracted.py" if parent.isEmpty && parent == "." { return generatedName } return FilePath(parent).appending(generatedName).string
entries.reason: The guard is `parent.isEmpty || parent == "."` and this mutant makes it `&&`, so the guard is always false and every file takes the fall-through. relativePath(of:under:) strips the root and its slash from a standardized URL path, so it never returns a path that starts with "./"; the parent is therefore never "." and the second term is dead. For a root-level file, FilePath.removingLastComponent() gives the empty path, and swift-system's FilePath.append(_: String) replaces an empty path with the appended one outright (`guard !isEmpty else { self = FilePath(other); return }`), so FilePath("").appending(generatedName).string is generatedName, exactly what the first branch returns. generatedName is the last path component plus a suffix, so it holds no separator that FilePath could reinterpret. Both versions produce the same path for every input. The `!=` candidate at this site IS observable and is killed by NestedJSONNotebookTests. Re-keyed from the old NSString text after the FilePath rewrite; the argument carries over. Survived in runs 39409099999 and 40494594871.

This mutant deletes the precondition in allRuntimeHelperFiles that traps when two languages claim the same helper filename. The input is fixed data: runtimeHelperFiles(for:) over AssignmentLanguage.allCases, and every filename it returns today is distinct. With no duplicate, the precondition never fires and the merged map is identical with or without it, so no test can observe the deletion. The trap guards a FUTURE edit, and if a duplicate is ever added, RuntimeSourceDriftTests (which calls allRuntimeHelperFiles) traps on the original code; that is when this entry stops holding and must be reconsidered. The 2026-09-22 before pass reported this KILLED by ScriptExecutionGapTests, which cannot depend on the deletion; the after pass reported it SURVIVED against run 35753274761.

This mutant deletes the fallback line in writeStructuredRunnerLog's guard-else, which writes a bare `{event, timestamp}` object when JSONSerialization cannot encode the payload. The guard cannot fail: every field value first passes through jsonSafeRunnerLogValue, which keeps a value only when `isValidJSONObject([value])` is true and otherwise replaces it with its description (#1932), recursing into dictionaries and arrays; the two values the function adds are strings. A dictionary of String keys and individually valid values is a valid JSON object, so `isValidJSONObject(payload)` holds, `data(withJSONObject:)` does not throw, and its output is UTF-8. No field a caller can pass reaches the else branch, so deleting its write changes nothing any test can observe. RunnerLogEventTests pins the behaviour that makes this true (a Date and a NaN both yield a full line). Verified SURVIVED against run 38402578905.

Awards( achievements: p.achievements.isEmpty ? nil : p.achievements, disabledBuiltIns: p.disabledBuiltInAwardIDs.isEmpty ? nil : p.disabledBuiltInAwardIDs) : nil
entries.reason: The site is `let hasAwards = p.builtInAchievementsSeeded || !p.achievements.isEmpty || !p.disabledBuiltInAwardIDs.isEmpty`, and this mutant makes the second `||` an `&&`, so it differs from the original only when builtInAchievementsSeeded is false and exactly one of achievements and disabledBuiltInAwardIDs is non-empty. ManifestV2.init(_:) has one caller, TestProperties.v2Envelope(), which encodes the envelope, decodes it, and keeps it only when the decoded value equals the input. The decoder sets builtInAchievementsSeeded to `awards != nil`. In the differing case the original writes an `awards` block, which decodes as seeded == true, not false; the mutant writes none, which decodes with the non-empty list empty. Either way the round trip differs from the input and v2Envelope() returns nil, so every manifest that reaches the site gets the same answer from both versions. The first-connector candidate at this site is killed by the builtInAchievementsSeeded-only case of ManifestV2Tests.v2RoundTripsExactly. Survived in run 39409099999.

entries.mutated: let submissionFiles = regularFiles(in: submissionDirectory) var progress = NormalizationProgress() // The student's own files must not be able to replace the tests they // are about to be graded by (#1357). Same guard the generic merge path // applies, because this path writes into the same workspace. let protected = protectedWorkspaceFilenames(manifest: manifest) writeStructuredRunnerLog( event: "submission_normalization_start", fields: [ "submission_directory": submissionDirectory.path, "workspace_directory": workspaceDirectory.path, "submission_filename": submissionFilename ?? "", "file_count": submissionFiles.count, ]) // The types of every file the loop below will classify, from one // `file` run rather than one per file. A file the batch could not // type is typed on its own in the loop, as every file used to be. let candidates = submissionFiles.indices.filter { !protected.contains(submissionFiles[$0].relativePath) } var batchedMimeTypes: [Int: String] = [:] if candidates.count < 1 { let detected = await mimeTypeDetector.detectMimeTypes(for: candidates.map { submissionFiles[$0].url }) for (index, mimeType) in zip(candidates, detected) { batchedMimeTypes[index] = mimeType } } for (index, file) in submissionFiles.enumerated() { let fileRelativePath = file.relativePath guard !protected.contains(fileRelativePath) else { progress.warnings.append(protectedFileSkippedWarning(fileRelativePath)) writeStructuredRunnerLog( event: "submission_file_refused", fields: [ "file": fileRelativePath, "reason": "belongs_to_test_setup", ]) continue } try await processSubmissionFile( file, knownMimeType: batchedMimeTypes[index], workspaceDirectory: workspaceDirectory, progress: &progress ) } try ensureProducedPythonFiles( progress: progress, submissionFiles: submissionFiles, workspaceDirectory: workspaceDirectory ) try applyCompatibilityCopyIfNeeded( manifest: manifest, workspaceDirectory: workspaceDirectory, progress: &progress ) writeStructuredRunnerLog( event: "submission_normalization_completed", fields: [ "workspace_directory": workspaceDirectory.path, "produced_python_files": progress.producedPythonFiles.map { relativePath(of: $0, under: workspaceDirectory) }, "warning_count": progress.warnings.count, ]) return NormalizationResult( warnings: progress.warnings, producedPythonFiles: progress.producedPythonFiles, preferredStudentModule: progress.preferredStudentModule )
entries.reason: The site is `if candidates.count > 1` in normalizePythonSubmission, which decides whether to type the submission's files with one batched `file` run before the per-file loop. This mutant makes it `< 1`, which is true only when there are no candidates, and detectMimeTypes([]) spawns nothing and returns []. So the mutant never batches, and every file reaches processSubmissionFile with knownMimeType nil, which types it with detectMimeType(for:) -- the per-file path the batch replaced and still falls back to for any file the batch could not type. The two paths run the same command (`file --mime-type -b`) on the same unmodified files and read each line with the same mimeType(fromOutput:); `file` prints a path's type independently of the other paths, and a batch whose exit code or line count is off is discarded (nil per file, then the per-file path). The batch is a spawn-count optimisation with no result of its own: the normalizer exposes no detector seam and logs nothing that names which path typed a file, so the workspace, the warnings, producedPythonFiles and preferredStudentModule are identical either way. The original's branch for exactly one candidate is the same argument: it skips the batch and types that file on its own. Verified SURVIVED against run 42829051616 (shard 9).

entries.mutated: let formatter = ISO8601DateFormatter() formatter.formatOptions = fractionalSeconds ? [.withInternetDateTime] : [.withInternetDateTime, .withFractionalSeconds] return formatter
entries.reason: formatter(fractionalSeconds:) is private to LiveSessionWindow and has exactly one caller, parse(_:), which evaluates `formatter(fractionalSeconds: false).date(from: iso) ?? formatter(fractionalSeconds: true).date(from: iso)`. Swapping the ternary swaps which options each argument value builds, so the mutant evaluates the same two formatters in the opposite order: `B ?? A` instead of `A ?? B`. Those differ only for a string that BOTH formatters accept with different instants. The two accept disjoint sets: `.withInternetDateTime` alone refuses any fractional part, and adding `.withFractionalSeconds` makes a fraction required. Measured with the toolchain the sweep uses (Swift 6.4, swift-foundation on Linux) over whole seconds, `.5`, `.000`, `.123456`, offsets with and without a fraction, a bare trailing `.`, a comma fraction, a missing seconds field, a space separator, no zone and trailing junk: no input parsed under both, so for every string one side of `??` is nil and both orders return the same Date, or both nil. format(_:) does not use these formatters (it calls iso8601String). Verified SURVIVED against run 42829051616 (shard 6).

applyToCellSource builds `rewritten` from `originalSource` by replacing each matched `{{name}}` with `substitutions[name]`, and it inserts `name` into `substituted` exactly when it replaces. So a changed text implies a non-empty `substituted`, and the `||` and `&&` forms disagree only when a substitution happened but left the text byte-identical: `substitutions[name] == "{{name}}"`. The only producer of `substitutions` that reaches this function is PersonalizationSubstitution's resolution (NotebookWorkingCopyStore and RunnerValidationService both pass `resolution.substitutions`), which holds `language.literal(value)` for static inputs and evaluated literals for per-student expressions, and `name` must pass isValidSharedName at save. No literal can equal `{{name}}` for a valid name: a string literal is quoted in every language; Python, R and Racket never open a literal with `{{`; an Octave cell renders a non-numeric element, which is quoted, a `containers.Map(...)` or another container; and a Lua `{{x}}` puts a bare `true`, `false`, a number or `chickadee.NULL` inside, none of which is a valid Lua identifier. The sibling mutant at this site (`!=` to `==`) is observable and is killed by NotebookSubstitutionCellShapeTests. Verified SURVIVED by hand on 2026-11-14 against the 151 database-free APITests suites of the local mutation run on NotebookSubstitution.swift and TestScriptVariablePrepender.swift.
